meme.take: Netflix released twenty episodes at once, a generous gift to anyone without plans.

story.next: Watch for whether either show reaches Netflix's weekly top 10.
story.summary: Both series arrived in full on October 15, alongside ABC's 9-1-1 and Grey's Anatomy premieres.
story.title: Netflix drops The Diplomat season 4 and Victorious spin-off Hollywood Arts
story.why: A big Thursday of returning shows gives streamers and networks a key autumn weekend.

story.background: Netflix is the world's largest paid streaming service. It added a cheaper ad-supported plan in 2022.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: Quarterly revenue reached $12.87 billion.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Ad sales are running behind Netflix's own target.

drivers.label: Controversy
drivers.text: It follows layoffs and the exits of senior executives.

story.happened: Net income rose 44% to $3.66 billion, Stock Titan reports. Netflix now expects about $2.7 billion in 2026 ad revenue, down from about $3 billion. Co-CEO Greg Peters said some areas had grown too fast, after its biggest job cuts since 2022.

meme.take: Netflix made more money than expected and still had to explain itself. Streaming is hard.

story.next: Watch for the ad tier's launch in 15 new countries in 2027, starting in March.
story.summary: Revenue rose 12% to $12.87 billion, yet Netflix lowered its 2026 ad revenue outlook and the stock fell about 6% after hours.
story.title: Netflix beats forecasts but cuts its ad sales goal, and its shares slide
story.why: Netflix sets the tone for streaming, and its ad business is meant to be its next big engine of growth.

story.background: Norm Macdonald was a Canadian comedian who anchored SNL's Weekend Update and died in 2021.

drivers.label: Nostalgia
drivers.text: His Weekend Update years on SNL are still widely shared.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Macdonald is regarded by many comedians as one of the best.

story.happened: Norm: The Tale of Norm Macdonald premiered on Netflix on October 16. It is built entirely from archival footage, personal photos and home videos, tracing his career from Saturday Night Live onward.

meme.take: Netflix let Norm Macdonald tell his own story, which was always the safest option.

story.next: Watch for reactions from fellow comedians and fans.
story.summary: Norm: The Tale of Norm Macdonald tells the comedian's story entirely through archive footage, photos and home videos.
story.title: Netflix releases an archive-only Norm Macdonald documentary
story.why: Macdonald remains one of the most admired stand-ups, with a devoted following online.

story.background: Oasis split in 2009 after a backstage fight between brothers Liam and Noel Gallagher.

drivers.label: Nostalgia
drivers.text: Oasis were one of the defining British bands of the 1990s.

drivers.label: Fan demand
drivers.text: The reunion tour sold out stadiums.

story.happened: Oasis: Don't Look Back in Anger is a two-hour documentary now on Disney+. It follows Liam and Noel Gallagher's Oasis Live '25 reunion tour and the fans who attended.

meme.take: The Oasis documentary proves the brothers can share a stage, and now a streaming service.

story.next: Watch for reactions from fans who were at the shows.
story.summary: Don't Look Back in Anger follows the Gallagher brothers' Oasis Live '25 tour and the fans who went.
story.title: Oasis reunion tour documentary arrives on Disney+
story.why: The reunion was one of the biggest music events of 2025, ending a split that lasted since 2009.

story.background: Blumhouse is a production company known for low-budget horror hits. Universal is one of Hollywood's major studios.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: A horror release in October has the calendar on its side.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: It took more than its $19 million budget in three days.

drivers.label: Controversy
drivers.text: A D+ CinemaScore means opening-night audiences did not like it.

story.happened: Universal and Blumhouse's Other Mommy opened to $27.5 million and $45 million worldwide, TheWrap reports. Its D+ CinemaScore is the lowest since Megalopolis. Verity fell 64% to about $11.5 million in its second weekend, and Resident Evil was third.

meme.take: Other Mommy proves people will pay good money to be disappointed, if it's scary.

story.next: Watch for how far it falls this weekend against Street Fighter, given its weak audience score.
story.summary: The Jessica Chastain horror film took $27.5 million on a $19 million budget despite a D+ audience grade.
story.title: Other Mommy opens at No. 1 with $27.5 million
story.why: October is horror season, and an original film leading the chart is a useful sign for cinemas.

story.background: Practical Magic was a 1998 film about witch sisters, based on Alice Hoffman's novel.

drivers.label: Nostalgia
drivers.text: It revisits a 1998 fan favorite.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman return.

story.happened: Practical Magic 2 became available to rent or buy on digital platforms including Prime Video and Apple TV, ComingSoon reports. Warner Bros. moved it to home viewing after a run that Yahoo reports passed $100 million.

meme.take: Practical Magic 2 made its money in cinemas. Now it haunts your rental queue.

story.next: Watch for when it reaches HBO Max for subscribers.
story.summary: The Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman sequel is now available to rent or buy on digital stores.
story.title: Practical Magic 2 arrives on digital after its box office run
story.why: The sequel came 28 years after the original, which built a large fan base on home video.

story.background: Resident Evil is Capcom's survival horror game series, adapted for film many times since 2002.

drivers.label: Nostalgia
drivers.text: Resident Evil has been a hit game series since 1996.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Video game films have become reliable box office earners.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: It is past $361 million worldwide.

story.happened: Resident Evil took RMB 62.5 million ($9.3M) in China, for $55.8M there since October 5, One Mann's Movies reports. It was third worldwide on the weekend with $22.6M. China's box office is $4.67B for the year, down 29.2% on 2025.

meme.take: Resident Evil is No. 1 in China for a second weekend. The undead have excellent staying power.

story.next: Watch for how it holds against new releases in China and whether it reaches $400 million worldwide.
story.summary: The film led China's box office for a second weekend with $9.3 million, as the country's yearly takings run 29% behind 2025.
story.title: Resident Evil holds No. 1 in China and passes $361 million worldwide
story.why: It is one of the year's biggest video game films, and China is a key market for Hollywood.

story.background: Riehle began his screen career in the John Wayne film Rooster Cogburn.

drivers.label: Nostalgia
drivers.text: Office Space became a cult favourite about office life.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: He appeared in more than 400 projects.

story.happened: Riehle died on Thursday and his representatives confirmed it on Monday, One Mann's Movies reports. His credits include Glory, Casino, The Fugitive, Free Willy and Bridesmaids, and he played Santa Claus in eight projects.

meme.bottom: And every one of them remembered
meme.take: Hollywood remembers a character actor who made small parts impossible to forget.

story.next: Watch for tributes from colleagues and screenings of his best-known films.
story.summary: Riehle, who worked on more than 400 projects over nearly five decades, died of natural causes in Los Angeles.
story.title: Character actor Richard Riehle, Office Space's Tom Smykowski, dies at 78
story.why: His face is familiar to millions from decades of film and TV roles, especially in Office Space.

story.background: Chris Evans is best known as Captain America in Marvel's films.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Chris Evans and Anya Taylor-Joy have large fan bases.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: It landed on a busy weekend for streaming releases.

story.happened: Sacrifice premiered on Netflix on October 16 and ranked second among Netflix films in the US on October 18, per FlixPatrol. Evans plays a fading star taken hostage by a radical leader played by Taylor-Joy.

meme.bottom: Calls it his best role in years
meme.take: In Sacrifice a fading star is kidnapped by a cult. His agent counts it as a booking.
meme.top: A movie star is taken hostage

story.next: Watch for whether it enters Netflix's global top 10 this week.
story.summary: Netflix's hostage comedy, about a movie star taken captive by a cult at a charity gala, is its second most-watched US film.
story.title: Chris Evans and Anya Taylor-Joy's Sacrifice climbs to No. 2 on Netflix
story.why: Two well-known leads made it one of the most visible streaming films of the weekend.

story.background: Sense and Sensibility is Jane Austen's 1811 novel, filmed most famously in 1995 with Emma Thompson.

drivers.label: Nostalgia
drivers.text: Austen adaptations have a loyal audience.

drivers.label: Fan demand
drivers.text: An A- CinemaScore points to strong word of mouth.

story.happened: Sense and Sensibility placed fifth for the weekend with about $7.25 million, Boxoffice Pro reports. Audiences gave it an A- CinemaScore. The 1995 version earned $43.18 million in North America.

meme.bottom: Then got an A- from the audience
meme.take: Two centuries on, Austen still opens modestly and wins on manners.

story.next: Watch for how it holds in coming weekends on word of mouth.
story.summary: Focus Features' Jane Austen adaptation took an estimated $7.25 million from 2,545 theaters, with audiences rating it highly.
story.title: New Sense and Sensibility opens to $7.25 million with an A- CinemaScore
story.why: Period dramas rarely open big, but strong audience scores can keep them running for weeks.

story.background: Aaron Sorkin won an Academy Award for writing The Social Network.

drivers.label: Nostalgia
drivers.text: The Social Network is one of the most acclaimed films of its decade.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Forecasts sit well below what the original opened to.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: Its subject, Facebook's parent company Meta, is still in the news every week.

story.happened: The Social Reckoning took $5.5 million in its opening weekend, TheWrap reports, less than a third of The Social Network's $22.6 million start. It earned a B- CinemaScore and has a reported net budget of about $30 million from Sony and Alcon.

meme.take: The Facebook sequel opened like an old account: still there, few people checking in.

story.next: Watch for whether awards attention helps its run in the coming weeks.
story.summary: Aaron Sorkin's follow-up to The Social Network opened fifth, below a third of the original's 2010 debut.
story.title: The Social Reckoning opens to $5.5 million in fifth place
story.why: It follows a much-loved film and tackles a company that is still in the headlines.

story.background: Street Fighter is Capcom's long-running fighting game series, first adapted for film in 1994.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Recent game films lost about two-thirds of their audience in week two.

drivers.label: Nostalgia
drivers.text: Street Fighter II was one of the defining arcade games of the 1990s.

story.happened: Paramount's Street Fighter opened to $30.77 million from 3,575 screens, Boxoffice Pro says. It forecasts $8 million to $13 million this weekend, citing drops of 62% to 69% for recent game films such as Resident Evil.

meme.bottom: Round two goes to the calendar
meme.take: Street Fighter won its opening bout. Second weekends are a different opponent.
meme.top: Round one went to Street Fighter

story.next: Watch for the size of its second-weekend drop against Clayface and Wildwood.
story.summary: Boxoffice Pro forecasts $8 million to $13 million for Street Fighter's second weekend.
story.title: Street Fighter faces a steep second weekend after its $31 million debut
story.why: Game adaptations have opened big this year but often fall fast in week two.

story.background: The Billboard 200 ranks the most popular albums in the US each week, combining sales and streams.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Swift is one of the best-selling artists in the world.

drivers.label: Record
drivers.text: No solo act had reached 100 weeks at No. 1 before.

drivers.label: Fan demand
drivers.text: An expanded Encore edition added four new songs.

story.happened: The Life of a Showgirl earned 93,000 units to lead the Billboard 200 for a 14th week, Billboard reports. That gives Swift 100 weeks at No. 1 across 15 albums, behind the Beatles' 132. The Beatles' Rubber Soul also returned to No. 4.

meme.take: The all-time chart race is close, and one side stopped recording in 1970.

story.next: Watch for whether the album extends its run on next week's chart.
story.summary: The Life of a Showgirl spent a 14th week atop the Billboard 200, leaving only the Beatles ahead of her on the all-time list.
story.title: Taylor Swift becomes the first solo act with 100 weeks at No. 1
story.why: It is a rare chart record, and only one act in history has more weeks at the top.

story.background: The Billboard 200 ranks the most popular albums in the US each week by sales and streams.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Swift is the biggest-selling artist of the decade.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Her career total passed 100 weeks at No. 1.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: Rodrigo and Wallen are close behind.

story.happened: The Life of a Showgirl earned 87,000 equivalent album units in the week ending October 15, down 7%. A physical restock on Swift's web store lifted album sales 38%. Olivia Rodrigo is No. 2 and Morgan Wallen No. 3.

meme.take: The Billboard 200 has become a weekly chart with one fixed answer and four guesses.

story.next: Watch for whether a new release can end Swift's run in the coming weeks.
story.summary: Swift's album earned 87,000 units for its 15th week at No. 1 on the Billboard 200.
story.title: Taylor Swift's The Life of a Showgirl spends a 15th week at No. 1
story.why: Fifteen weeks on top is a rare run for any album in the streaming era.

story.background: A trademark protects names, logos or sounds that identify a brand. Voices have rarely been registered.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Swift is one of the world's best-selling artists.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: AI voice clones of famous singers spread easily online.

drivers.label: First of its kind
drivers.text: A lawyer called voice trademarks a new use of the law.

story.happened: TAS Rights Management filed sound marks in the UK and EU on October 6, Music Business Worldwide reports. IP Australia accepted one for "Hey, it's Taylor Swift" on October 12. Three US applications were filed in April.

meme.bottom: The AI covers need a licence now
meme.take: Taylor Swift is trademarking her voice abroad, a sentence that once made no sense.

story.next: Watch for the Australian opposition period and the UK and EU examiners' decisions.
story.summary: Swift's company has filed sound marks for recordings of her voice abroad, following US filings, as artists push back on AI deepfakes.
story.title: Taylor Swift files to trademark her voice in the UK, EU and Australia
story.why: Using trademark law to protect a voice is untested, and other artists may follow if it works.

story.background: Prime Video is Amazon's streaming service. The Terminal List first premiered in 2022.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Chris Pratt leads the series.

drivers.label: Source material
drivers.text: It is based on Jack Carr's bestselling thriller novels.

story.happened: Chris Pratt returns as Navy SEAL James Reece in the eight-episode second season. Tom's Guide describes it as a conspiracy story that stretches from Moscow to Langley.

meme.bottom: The conspiracy now needs a passport
meme.take: Season 2 runs from Moscow to Langley. The conspiracy has upgraded its air miles.

story.next: Watch for Prime Video's viewing figures for the new season.
story.summary: Season 2 of the action thriller premiered on October 21 with eight episodes, Tom's Guide reports.
story.title: The Terminal List returns to Prime Video with Chris Pratt
story.why: Action thrillers based on bestselling novels are a reliable draw for streamers.

story.background: True Detective is HBO's crime anthology series. Each season has a new cast and story.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Nicolas Cage and Antonio Banderas are both well-known film stars.

drivers.label: Nostalgia
drivers.text: The first season set a high bar for prestige TV.

story.happened: Banderas will play Rai Garcia and Cage will play Henry Logan, Deadline reports. Issa López, who wrote and directed season 4, returns as showrunner. Production begins in 2027.

meme.bottom: The swamp has met its match
meme.take: HBO cast Nicolas Cage in a bleak crime drama, a genre about to become slightly less bleak.

story.next: Watch for more casting and a release window from HBO.
story.summary: HBO confirmed the two stars for the next season, reportedly set in New York's Jamaica Bay, with filming in 2027.
story.title: Antonio Banderas and Nicolas Cage join True Detective season 5
story.why: True Detective's casting is always a talking point after its famous first season.

story.background: Tulsa King follows a New York mobster who builds a new operation in Oklahoma after prison.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Sylvester Stallone leads the series.

drivers.label: Fan demand
drivers.text: The show has been renewed season after season.

story.happened: Tulsa King's fourth season premiered on Paramount+ on October 16. Dwight works to legitimize his empire while facing corrupt politicians, new enemies and personal loss.

meme.take: Dwight tries to go straight for a fourth season, a pace familiar from most January plans.

story.next: Watch for weekly episodes and the streamer's viewing figures.
story.summary: Sylvester Stallone's mob drama returns as Dwight pushes his crew toward legitimate business.
story.title: Tulsa King season 4 premieres on Paramount+
story.why: Sylvester Stallone's crime drama has now run for four seasons on Paramount+.

story.background: Marvel Studios is owned by Disney and releases its series on Disney+. Vision first appeared in Avengers: Age of Ultron.

drivers.label: Fan demand
drivers.text: Marvel series still draw some of streaming's biggest audiences.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Paul Bettany has played Vision since 2015.

drivers.label: Controversy
drivers.text: Some critics found the season slow.

story.happened: VisionQuest premiered on Disney+ this week with mostly positive reviews, ComicBookMovie reports, citing a Fresh Rotten Tomatoes score at the review embargo. Critics praised Bettany and Spader, while some said the season spends too long on backstory. Terry Matalas co-wrote the series.

meme.take: In the Marvel universe, death is less an ending than a contract renegotiation.
meme.top: Vision died, came back, got a series

story.next: Watch for audience reaction and Disney+ viewing figures after the premiere.
story.summary: Paul Bettany returns as Vision, with James Spader's Ultron, in an eight-episode Disney+ series.
story.title: Marvel's VisionQuest premieres on Disney+ to mostly positive reviews
story.why: VisionQuest continues a story Marvel fans have followed since WandaVision.

story.background: Vision is the android Avenger first played by Paul Bettany in Avengers: Age of Ultron in 2015.

drivers.label: Fan demand
drivers.text: Vision's story was left open after WandaVision.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Paul Bettany and James Spader return to their Marvel roles.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: New episodes arrive weekly through the autumn.

story.happened: VisionQuest premiered on Disney+ on October 14 as an eight-episode limited series, with a 79% Certified Fresh score. Paul Bettany returns as Vision, who hides from those who want to weaponize him, with James Spader voicing Ultron.

meme.bottom: The AI is Ultron, so that's a choice
meme.take: Marvel's hero seeks life advice from Ultron, a classic case of asking the wrong group chat.
meme.top: Vision asks AI about his purpose

story.next: Watch for weekly episode reactions and any hints tying Vision to future Avengers films.
story.summary: The eight-episode series follows a rebooted Vision on the run, and critics call it clever but loosely tied to the wider MCU.
story.title: Marvel's VisionQuest lands on Disney+ with a 79% critics score
story.why: It is Marvel's latest bet on character-led streaming shows after the success of WandaVision.

story.background: Star Wars is owned by Disney through Lucasfilm. Waititi also directed an episode of The Mandalorian.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Waititi directed Thor: Ragnarok and Jojo Rabbit.

drivers.label: Fan demand
drivers.text: Star Wars fans have waited years for new films.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Several announced Star Wars films have stalled.

story.happened: Waititi told Inverse, while promoting Klara and the Sun, that the film is on hold, The Playlist reports. Lucasfilm announced it in May 2020, and Kathleen Kennedy said in January that he had delivered a script. Waititi did not rule out a return.

meme.take: Lucasfilm now has enough paused Star Wars films to fill a galaxy reasonably far away.
meme.top: Taika's Star Wars film is on ice

story.next: Watch for any comment from Lucasfilm on the film's status.
story.summary: The director says the film announced in 2020 is on hold as he and writer Tony McNamara move to another project.
story.title: Taika Waititi says his Star Wars film is 'very iced'
story.why: It is one more Star Wars film that has stalled, leaving fans unsure which announced projects will be made.

story.background: Whalefall is based on Daniel Kraus's 2023 novel and released by 20th Century Studios.

drivers.label: First of its kind
drivers.text: A story set inside a whale is an unusual premise.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: It opened against Street Fighter.

story.happened: Whalefall placed fourth with about $8 million from 3,065 theaters and a B CinemaScore, Boxoffice Pro reports. It added $9.5 million internationally for a $17.5 million global start against a reported $60 million budget.

meme.take: A film about being swallowed whole opened against Street Fighter. It knows the feeling.
meme.top: A film about life inside a whale

story.next: Watch for its overseas results and second weekend drop.
story.summary: Disney's survival thriller took about $8 million in North America and $9.5 million overseas, short of expectations.
story.title: Whalefall opens fourth with $8 million
story.why: Original thrillers struggle for attention when franchise films share the weekend.

story.background: Laika is the Oregon studio behind Coraline and Kubo and the Two Strings. Colin Meloy leads the band The Decemberists.

drivers.label: Fan demand
drivers.text: Critics are calling it one of Laika's best, a studio with a loyal following.

drivers.label: First of its kind
drivers.text: Stop-motion films on this scale take years to make by hand.

story.happened: Wildwood opens in the US on October 23 through Fathom Entertainment. Boxoffice Pro lists it at 100% with critics and 98% with audiences on Rotten Tomatoes. Variety calls it Laika's most ambitious feature yet.

meme.bottom: Reviewed one rave at a time
meme.take: Laika spent years moving puppets by hand. Critics replied at the same pace, unanimously.
meme.top: Made one frame at a time

story.next: Watch for its opening weekend and whether it joins the animated film awards race.
story.summary: Travis Knight's adaptation of the Colin Meloy novel opens October 23 with a 100% Rotten Tomatoes critics' score.
story.title: Laika's stop-motion epic Wildwood opens with perfect early reviews
story.why: Laika makes some of the most admired animated films, and big stop-motion releases are rare.

story.background: Elizabeth Holmes founded the blood-testing company Theranos and was convicted of fraud in 2022.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: About 70% of its opening audience was under 35, Boxoffice Pro reports.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: It is going head to head with DC's Clayface this weekend.

story.happened: The film opened to $15.6 million from 855 screens with over 2,000 sellouts, Boxoffice Pro says, and topped Wednesday's box office, Deadline reports. It expands on October 23, with a weekend forecast of $15 million to $20 million.

meme.take: Elizabeth Holmes promised results nobody could verify. Nathan Fielder delivered $15 million.

story.next: Watch for whether it tops Clayface for the weekend once it reaches more than 2,500 screens.
story.summary: After a $15.6 million start from 855 screens, A24's You Can See Everything expands to 2,500+ screens on Friday.
story.title: Nathan Fielder's Holmes film goes wide after winning Wednesday's box office
story.why: A comedian's documentary-style film is drawing young crowds and could beat a superhero film this weekend.

story.background: YouTube Music is Google's music streaming service, launched in 2018.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: AI-generated music is growing fast on streaming platforms.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: Spotify, Deezer and Apple Music are taking different approaches.

drivers.label: Controversy
drivers.text: Artists worry about AI tracks competing for royalties.

story.happened: YouTube Music is adding three labels: Fully Gen AI, Partly Gen AI and No Gen AI, TechCrunch reports. Unlike Deezer and Tidal, it will not remove AI tracks from recommendations or royalties. Spotify already labels AI music, and Apple Music plans tags later this year.

meme.take: YouTube Music will now tell you when a song had no human involved, in case the lyrics didn't.

story.next: Watch for how labels are applied and whether YouTube changes how AI songs are paid.
story.summary: Tracks will be tagged Fully Gen AI, Partly Gen AI or No Gen AI, but AI songs stay in recommendations.
story.title: YouTube Music adds labels for AI-generated songs
story.why: AI-made songs are flooding streaming services, and listeners want to know what they are hearing.

story.background: Alex Garland wrote and directed Ex Machina and Civil War. A24 is a US film studio.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Zendaya stars in Dune and Spider-Man films.

drivers.label: Fan demand
drivers.text: Garland's films reliably draw sci-fi fans.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: A24 keeps landing major stars for original films.

story.happened: Zendaya has signed on to Alex Garland's untitled sci-fi film for A24, Dark Horizons reports, citing Variety. Filming is planned for next year. It is her third A24 project after Euphoria and The Drama, and follows Garland's Elden Ring adaptation.

meme.take: Hollywood now announces films with no title or plot, and they still trend.

story.next: Watch for a title, more casting and a plot description.
story.summary: The untitled film, with plot under wraps, is set to shoot next year, Variety reports.
story.title: Zendaya joins Alex Garland's next sci-fi film at A24
story.why: It pairs one of Hollywood's biggest young stars with the director of Ex Machina and Civil War.

story.background: Steam is Valve's PC game store, where free demos help small studios find an audience.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: AI coding tools have made it fast to copy simple games.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Studios may stop releasing demos to protect their ideas.

drivers.label: Controversy
drivers.text: Developers disagree on how much AI use is fair.

story.happened: At least seven Roblox clones of Escape the Walls appeared within nine days, PC Gamer reports. Alliance Arts cancelled its Drunken Goddess Reflux demo over fears of AI copies. NoGlyph says another game copied its Needle In A Haystack code and has filed a notice with Valve.

meme.take: Indie developers have found the perfect protection against copying: never showing anyone.
meme.top: A studio made a new game

story.next: Watch for how Valve handles the Needle In A Haystack copyright notice.
story.summary: PC Gamer reports quick AI-built copies of new indie hits, with one studio cancelling its Steam demo for fear of clones.
story.title: AI-made clone games are pushing indie developers to hide their demos
story.why: If a demo can be copied in days, small studios lose their main way to find players.

story.background: ARC Raiders is an online extraction shooter from Embark Studios, a Swedish studio owned by Nexon.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: 185,000 concurrent players is a big count on Steam.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: A free week brought in many new players.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: It comes before a crowded run of new shooters.

story.happened: The free Frozen Trail update on October 8 added a new map and three enemy types, and the game was free to play from October 8 to 12. On October 11 it passed 185,000 concurrent Steam players, its highest since March 2026, according to SteamDB figures.

meme.take: The most effective marketing in gaming remains not charging anything for five days.
meme.top: ARC Raiders went free for a week

story.next: Watch for whether player numbers hold now the free week is over.
story.summary: Embark's shooter hit its highest Steam player count since March after a free update and a free-to-play week.
story.title: ARC Raiders bounces back to 185,000 Steam players after its Frozen Trail update
story.why: A big comeback for a struggling online game shows a strong update can win players back.

story.background: Assassin's Creed is Ubisoft's historical action series. Tencent is a major investor in Ubisoft.

drivers.label: Fan demand
drivers.text: Ancient China has long been a requested setting.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Assassin's Creed is Ubisoft's biggest series.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Cancelled projects point to wider cutbacks in the industry.

story.happened: MP1st first reported the footage, which shows a female assassin in the Qin Dynasty around 206 BCE and a boss fight with Xiang Yu, VGC reports. The game was reportedly planned for console and PC before being cancelled.

meme.bottom: They got a trailer for a cancelled one
meme.take: Assassin's Creed finally visited ancient China, briefly, in someone's portfolio.

story.background: Capcom is the Japanese publisher behind Resident Evil, Monster Hunter and Street Fighter.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: More than 11 million accounts are reported to be affected.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Exposed emails and login IDs can be used in phishing attempts.

story.happened: Capcom spotted suspicious activity on October 19 and reported it to Osaka police and Japan's privacy regulator on October 21. Exposed data includes emails, IP addresses and login IDs; 196 accounts had passwords changed without permission. Capcom says card data was not affected.

story.background: Castlevania is Konami's series about the Belmont family's fight against Dracula, first released in 1986.

drivers.text: Castlevania is one of gaming's oldest action series.

drivers.text: Fans have waited years for a new entry.

meme.take: Dracula rules Paris in the new Castlevania. The locals have survived worse rent.

story.next: Watch for sales figures and whether Konami revives more of its classic series.

drivers.text: Sony gained while Nintendo and Xbox fell.

drivers.text: Average console prices rose sharply from a year ago.

story.happened: US hardware unit sales fell 3% in September, Circana data shows, Pure Xbox reports. PS5 rose 22%, Switch 2 fell 14% and Xbox Series fell 27%, a new September low. The average price paid for an Xbox rose 33% to $663.

meme.take: Xbox raised prices and sold fewer consoles. Economists can finally stop arguing about this.

story.next: Watch for October's figures, which will include Modern Warfare 4's launch.
story.summary: Circana's September figures show PS5 up 22%, Switch 2 down 14% and Xbox Series down 27% from a year ago.

story.background: BioWare was founded in 1995 in Edmonton and bought by EA in 2007. Its last game was Dragon Age: The Veilguard in 2024.

drivers.text: The buyout added about $18 billion in debt, and EA has promised big savings.

story.happened: BioWare said early work on the next Mass Effect is ending. Bloomberg reports EA will cut about 400 jobs, roughly 3% of staff, including about 50 at BioWare. It follows EA's $55 billion buyout led by Saudi Arabia's PIF, which left about $18 billion in debt.

meme.take: BioWare spent 30 years making player choices matter. EA made one this week.

meme.top: Game Pass is going a la carte

story.next: Watch for Microsoft confirming new tiers and prices, and any further Xbox job cuts.
story.summary: Fortune reports players could pick features like cloud play and multiplayer separately in a tiered Game Pass.
story.title: Xbox is reported to be planning an a la carte Game Pass
story.why: Game Pass is Xbox's biggest bet, and this would change what millions of subscribers pay for.

story.background: Xbox Cloud Gaming lets Game Pass Ultimate members stream games to TVs, phones and headsets.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Xbox is pushing cloud play on screens without a console.

story.happened: Microsoft announced the Xbox Nano controller on October 14 for $49.99, with preorders open and shipping in November, Thurrott reports. It weighs about 3.5 ounces, has a replaceable battery and works over Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. Select Samsung TVs and Meta Quest headsets will bundle it in the US.

meme.bottom: Your hands stayed the same size
meme.take: The Xbox Nano fits in a pocket, which is also where most controllers go missing.

story.next: Watch for hands-on impressions and which markets get it first in November.
story.summary: The smallest Xbox controller yet is just over five inches long and ships in select markets in November.
story.title: Microsoft unveils the $49.99 Xbox Nano, a pocket-sized controller
story.why: A cheap, small controller fits Xbox's push to play on TVs, headsets and phones, not just consoles.

story.background: Microsoft bought Activision Blizzard for about $69 billion in 2023, making Xbox one of the largest game publishers.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Fortune reports some staff believe Xbox could be readied for a sale or spinoff.

story.happened: The Information reports private equity firms discussed a buyout and valued Xbox at $100 billion to $150 billion, Pure Xbox says. The talks were short-lived. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has said Xbox is not for sale.

meme.bottom: But someone checked the price anyway
meme.take: Private equity valued Xbox at up to $150 billion. Microsoft would like people to stop asking.

story.next: Watch for any further statement from Microsoft on Xbox's future inside the company.
story.summary: The Information reports brief, exploratory buyout talks about Xbox that never reached Microsoft as a formal offer.
story.title: Private equity firms are said to have valued Xbox at $100-150 billion
story.why: Any hint that Microsoft could sell Xbox would reshape the console business.

story.background: The Legend of Zelda is Nintendo's fantasy adventure series, first released in 1986.

drivers.label: Nostalgia
drivers.text: The original came out on the Nintendo 64 in 1998.

drivers.label: Fan demand
drivers.text: Zelda remakes are among Nintendo's top sellers.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: It lands two weeks before GTA VI.

story.happened: Nintendo released an overview trailer with about five minutes of gameplay from the Ocarina of Time remake, Simulation Daily reports. A new area, the Hall of Fallen Foes, lets players re-fight bosses. It launches November 5 on Switch 2 and works with the Zelda Notes app.

meme.take: Nintendo remade Ocarina of Time, and somehow the boss fights are now optional reruns.

story.next: Watch for reviews ahead of the November 5 launch.
story.summary: The Switch 2 remake adds a boss-rematch area and arrives on November 5.
story.title: Nintendo shows five minutes of its Ocarina of Time remake
story.why: Ocarina of Time is often named among the greatest games ever made.

drivers.label: Nostalgia
drivers.text: The Legend of Zelda turns 40 this year.

drivers.label: Fan demand
drivers.text: The special console has been selling out at retailers.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: Shortages are hitting just before the holidays.

story.happened: Bill van Zyll, Nintendo's Latin America chief, said the company underestimated demand and that restocks are coming but will take time, Nintendo Life reports. He singled out North America. The Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 arrives November 5.

meme.take: Nintendo underestimated demand for a Zelda console, which is a bold thing to underestimate.
meme.top: Nintendo thought Zelda fans could wait

story.next: Watch for restock dates and sales when the Ocarina of Time remake launches on November 5.
story.summary: A Nintendo executive apologised for shortages of the Zelda 40th Anniversary console and promised restocks, without a date.
story.title: Nintendo says it underestimated demand for its Zelda Switch 2 console
story.why: Shortages of a collector's console ahead of the holidays frustrate fans and hint at strong demand.

story.background: Ahold Delhaize is a Dutch-Belgian group that owns Albert Heijn, Delhaize, Food Lion, Stop & Shop and Hannaford.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: The group serves about 60 million customers a week.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: It hit the same weekend as attacks on French supermarkets.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Fresh food deliveries were disrupted.

story.happened: Ahold Delhaize took systems offline after a cybersecurity incident that began on October 11. Work stopped at several Albert Heijn distribution centers, NL Times reports, and Food Lion, Stop & Shop and Hannaford websites went down. Stores stayed open. Its shares fell 3.15%.

meme.take: A plain update: Ahold Delhaize's stores stayed open while its systems were restored.

story.next: Watch for how long restoration takes and whether customer data was affected.
story.summary: Albert Heijn warned of empty shelves as distribution centers stopped, and US chains' websites went down.
story.title: Ahold Delhaize takes systems offline after a cyber incident
story.why: The group runs thousands of grocery stores used by millions of shoppers each week.

story.background: Ahold Delhaize is a Dutch-Belgian retail group that owns Albert Heijn and several US grocery chains.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Albert Heijn is the largest supermarket chain in the Netherlands.

drivers.label: First of its kind
drivers.text: Police said they had never publicly asked a company to report a crime before.

story.happened: A cyberattack hit Ahold Delhaize's Albert Heijn chain this week, and logistics systems are being restored, with stock varying by store. Police said it was the first time they had publicly asked a company to file a complaint. The firm says there is no sign data was stolen.

meme.bottom: Police ask if anyone wants to report it
meme.take: Dutch police politely invite a hacked supermarket to mention it was hacked.

story.next: Watch for whether a criminal investigation opens and how fast stores return to normal.
story.summary: Dutch authorities publicly asked the supermarket group to file a criminal complaint after a cyberattack hit its logistics.
story.title: Cyberattack disrupts Albert Heijn as Dutch police urge Ahold Delhaize to report it
story.why: Attacks on supermarkets show how hacking can quickly affect everyday essentials.

story.background: AI agents are AI systems that can carry out multi-step tasks on a computer with little supervision.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: AI agents can scale up attacks cheaply.

drivers.label: First of its kind
drivers.text: It is among the clearest reported cases of agents running a hacking campaign.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Security teams are racing to adapt to AI-powered attackers.

story.happened: Reuters reports the hacker breached the websites of more than 100 companies, with AI agents doing much of the work and limited human involvement. The whole campaign reportedly cost only a few thousand dollars.

meme.bottom: The invoice was a few thousand dollars
meme.take: AI agents promised to make work cheaper for everyone. Everyone turned out to include hackers.

story.next: Watch for which companies were hit and how security firms respond to agent-driven attacks.
story.summary: A Chinese-speaking hacker handed much of the work to AI agents, with a campaign that reportedly cost a few thousand dollars.
story.title: One hacker used AI agents to breach more than 100 company websites, Reuters reports
story.why: Cheap, automated attacks could let one person do what once took a team of hackers.

story.background: Amazon makes Echo speakers, Kindle e-readers and Fire tablets, and runs the Alexa voice assistant.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: Apple unveiled its own smart home display the day before.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Alexa is one of the most used voice assistants.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: They arrive ahead of the holiday shopping season.

story.happened: Amazon's Alexa Tablet 8, 11 and 12 Pro became available on October 14 in the US, Mexico and Canada, Engadget reports. Prices start at $230, $330 and $500. The UK, Germany, France, Italy and Spain get them on October 19. A $249 Ring smart lock arrives early next year.

meme.bottom: Amazon launched three, the next day
meme.take: The smart home wars have reached the stage where every room needs a tablet and a lawyer.

story.next: Watch for reviews and how they compare with Apple's new HomeView.
story.summary: Three Alexa Tablet models arrived in the US, Mexico and Canada on October 14, with Europe following on October 19.
story.title: Amazon's new Alexa tablets go on sale in the US from $230
story.why: Amazon is putting Alexa at the center of its devices as rivals push smart home screens.

story.background: Amazon bought the AI wearable startup Bee and is now selling its devices under that brand.

drivers.label: Controversy
drivers.text: Devices that record conversations face privacy pushback.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: AI wearables are a new category big tech is racing into.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Amazon is backing the devices with its Alexa ecosystem.

story.happened: Bee Frontier costs $75 and Bee Eclipse, a magnetic phone add-on, costs $100, with integrations on a $12 monthly plan. A former AWS security engineer told GeekWire the devices have a problem with bystanders who never opted in.

meme.bottom: And writes it down for you, helpfully
meme.take: Amazon's Bee records your conversations, then kindly reminds you what you shouldn't have said.

story.next: Watch for privacy regulators' reaction and early reviews.
story.summary: The $75 Bee Frontier bracelet and $100 Bee Eclipse phone attachment turn conversations into summaries and to-do lists.
story.title: Amazon launches Bee AI wearables that listen to and summarize conversations
story.why: Always-listening devices raise fresh questions about recording people who never agreed to it.

story.background: Amazon runs AWS, the world's largest cloud computing business, as well as its online store.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: More than €16 billion in a single year.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Tech giants are building AI data centers across Europe.

story.happened: Amazon plans to invest more than €16 billion ($17.9B) in Germany in 2027, Bloomberg reports. The money spans AWS and AI data centers, its Leo satellite internet project, Prime Video production and a new robotics lab in Berlin.

meme.bottom: Germany has been asked to sign for it
meme.take: Amazon is spending €16 billion in Germany, with a delivery window of all of 2027.

story.next: Watch for where the new German data centers will be built.
story.summary: The plan covers AWS and AI data centers, the Leo satellite program, Prime Video productions and a Berlin robotics lab.
story.title: Amazon pledges more than €16 billion for Germany in 2027
story.why: It is a big bet on European AI computing as tech giants race to build data centers.

story.background: Apple reviews every app before it appears on the App Store, its iPhone app marketplace.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Nonconsensual deepfake images cause real harm to the people depicted.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Regulators worldwide are pressing platforms on AI abuse.

story.happened: MacRumors reports Apple updated guideline 1.2 to require apps to prevent and remove AI-generated nonconsensual intimate imagery. New guideline 2.5.19 targets apps that hide features during review and add nudify functions later.

meme.bottom: Apps that hide things get hidden
meme.take: Apple now bans apps that act innocent during review, ending a long tradition.
meme.top: Apple updated its App Store rules

story.next: Watch for apps being removed under the new rules.
story.summary: Developers must now prevent and remove AI-made nonconsensual intimate images, and apps that hide such features from reviewers are banned.
story.title: Apple's new App Store rules target AI deepfakes and 'nudify' apps
story.why: Nudify apps have spread fast, and app stores are under pressure to stop them.

story.background: Apple Home is Apple's app and platform for controlling smart home devices from an iPhone.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: Amazon and Google dominate smart displays and speakers.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Any new Apple product category draws wide attention.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: Commentators noted the higher prices of the new home devices.

story.happened: HomeView costs $299 and launches November 13, with the new Apple TV 4K at $299 and HomePod mini 2 at $149, MacRumors reports. Some tabletop HomeView colors now ship in early December, and Siri AI arrives in a later update.

meme.take: Apple's HomeView ships in November. The smarter Siri will follow when it is ready.
meme.top: Apple made a screen for your kitchen

story.next: Watch for reviews of HomeView and the accessories' shipping dates.
story.summary: Apple opened preorders for a 7-inch HomeView display, a new HomePod mini, Apple TV 4K and cameras, locks and thermostats.
story.title: Apple launches HomeView, a $300 smart display, with a wider smart home lineup
story.why: It is Apple's biggest push into the smart home, where Amazon and Google have long led.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: New Apple hardware draws wide attention.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: It would land just before the holiday season.

story.happened: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports new Macs arrive November 6, and 9to5Mac reports Apple's first touchscreen MacBook could debut then. An unreleased iPad mini Smart Folio, model A3632, appeared in a French regulatory database, Android Headlines reports.

meme.take: Apple's position on touchscreen Macs is reported to be evolving, as positions do.
meme.top: Apple said no to touchscreen Macs

story.next: Watch for an Apple announcement confirming the new Macs and iPad mini.
story.summary: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says new Macs arrive November 6, and a filing for an unreleased iPad mini case hints at a redesign.
story.title: New Macs are reported for November 6 as a new iPad mini case leaks
story.why: Apple's fall lineup is filling out after the iPhone Duo and HomeView launches.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: It comes days before the iPhone Duo goes on sale.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Tech firms are moving more manufacturing to the US.

story.happened: Apple is putting up to $100 million over three years into Perryman, which supplies titanium for the iPhone Duo, CNBC reports. It also expanded a camera parts partnership with Qnity. Apple says nearly 100 iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro parts are made in the US.

meme.bottom: It is spending $100 million to keep it
meme.take: Apple is putting $100 million into titanium. The iPhone Duo is partly made of investment.

story.next: Watch for more US supplier deals as Apple ramps up iPhone Duo production.

story.title: Apple commits up to $100 million to a US titanium supplier for the iPhone Duo
story.why: Apple is under pressure to make more of its products in the US.

story.background: Apple has kept touch to the iPhone and iPad, while many Windows laptops have touchscreens.

drivers.label: First of its kind
drivers.text: It would be the first Mac with a touchscreen.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: The showcase is reported for the end of October.

story.happened: Apple has invited media to an October 28 "Launch Experience," MacRumors reports, and a touchscreen MacBook Pro is rumored for as soon as November 6. Earlier, Macworld found Safari beta interface elements pointing to touch support.

meme.take: Apple prepares a touchscreen Mac, after years of explaining why nobody needed one.
meme.top: Apple said touchscreen Macs were wrong

story.next: Watch for Apple confirming an event date.
story.summary: New interface elements in Safari suggest macOS 27 is being readied for touch, as Apple is reported to plan a late-October showcase.
story.title: Safari beta hints at Apple's first touchscreen MacBook ahead of a reported event
story.why: A touchscreen Mac would reverse years of Apple saying touch did not belong on laptops.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: A new Apple product category always draws heavy coverage.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: Amazon and Google have sold smart displays for years.

drivers.label: Timing
drivers.text: It is one of two rounds of Apple launches reported for October.

story.happened: HomeView costs $299 and launches November 13 with an A18 chip and Siri AI, MacRumors reports. HomePod mini 2 is $149 from October 30, and a $299 Apple TV 4K with an A19 chip arrives November 13. HomeView will not be sold in the EU.

meme.bottom: Your fridge is the last holdout
meme.take: HomeView skips the EU, so Europe's kitchens stay blissfully un-onboarded.
meme.top: Apple built a screen for your kitchen

story.next: Watch for first reviews in November and the wall mount, sold separately from $59.
story.summary: Apple refreshed its smart home lineup on October 13 with a 7-inch HomeView display, HomePod mini 2 and a faster Apple TV.
story.title: Apple unveils the $299 HomeView hub, a new HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K
story.why: HomeView is Apple's long-rumored first smart display, taking on Amazon and Google.

story.background: ASML is a Dutch company and the sole maker of EUV lithography machines used for advanced chips.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: Record sales came with a higher full-year forecast.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: It plans 65 EUV and 130 immersion machines for 2027.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: AI chip demand is driving orders years ahead.

story.happened: ASML reported third-quarter sales of €11.66 billion and raised its 2026 revenue forecast to €44 to €45 billion, Investing.com reports. It is adding 30% capacity for EUV and immersion machines in 2027 and studying another 30% for 2028. Some customers want orders for 2029 and 2030.

meme.take: ASML's waiting list now runs into 2030, which is one way to plan for the future.

story.next: Watch for whether supply shortfalls ease as the new capacity comes online.
story.summary: The chip equipment maker posted record third-quarter sales and still expects supply shortfalls.
story.title: ASML lifts its 2026 forecast and adds 30% capacity as AI demand grows
story.why: ASML makes the only machines that print the most advanced chips, so its orders track the AI chip boom.

story.background: Barclays is a British bank with large retail and investment banking businesses.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: About 5,000 jobs, roughly 5% of the bank's staff.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Banks are among the first big employers to tie cuts to AI.

story.happened: Barclays disclosed the cuts with its third-quarter results, Business Insider reports. About 60% of affected roles are in support functions, including software development. Finance director Anna Cross said AI is raising productivity and changing the cost base.

meme.take: Barclays found AI boosts productivity. The reward is being distributed unevenly.

story.next: Watch for which countries and teams the cuts hit and whether other banks follow.
story.summary: The bank is cutting about 5% of its workforce, with roughly 60% of roles in support functions.
story.title: Barclays plans about 5,000 job cuts as AI raises productivity
story.why: It is one of the clearest cases of a big employer linking job cuts to AI.

story.background: BeyondTrust makes software IT teams use to access and support computers remotely.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: The flaw was used in attacks before a patch existed.

drivers.label: Rivalry
drivers.text: The attackers are described as China-linked.

story.happened: The Hacker News reports the Armory Castle group exploited CVE-2026-102764, rated 9.3, as a zero-day in late August. Cloud customers were patched by October 9, while self-hosted versions 24.3.1 to 26.2.3 need manual updates.

meme.take: BeyondTrust's remote support tool gave very remote support to people nobody had hired.

story.next: Watch for government advisories and reports of affected organizations.
story.summary: A flaw in BeyondTrust's remote support software was exploited before a fix, and self-hosted customers must update manually.
story.title: China-linked hackers exploited a BeyondTrust zero-day to seize support servers
story.why: Remote support tools can reach deep inside networks, making them prized targets.

story.background: The ballroom is a construction project at the White House funded by private donations.

drivers.label: Money
drivers.text: The combined total from six firms is $92 million.

drivers.label: Controversy
drivers.text: Corporate gifts to a White House project raise questions about influence.

story.happened: The Verge reports that Nvidia, Apple, Google, Microsoft, Amazon and Meta together contributed $92 million toward the White House ballroom.

meme.take: Big tech chipped in $92 million for a ballroom, the most they've agreed on in years.

story.next: Watch for more disclosure of donors and amounts.
story.summary: Nvidia, Apple, Google, Microsoft, Amazon and Meta together contributed $92 million to President Trump's ballroom project.
story.title: Six tech giants gave a combined $92 million toward the White House ballroom
story.why: Big donations from tech firms draw scrutiny as the same companies face government decisions on AI.

story.background: Bluesky is a social network built on the open AT Protocol.

drivers.label: Trend
drivers.text: Building apps by describing them to AI is spreading fast.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: Bluesky has 47 million registered users.

story.happened: Bluesky expanded its experimental Attie platform so anyone can build websites, quizzes, polls and small games, TechCrunch reports. Creators can plug in their own or open-weight models. CEO Toni Schneider called it social vibe coding, and work spreads across a network of 47 million users.

meme.take: Bluesky now lets users build apps, giving everyone a new way to never finish a side project.

story.next: Watch for what users build and how Bluesky handles moderation of AI-made apps.
story.summary: Users can now make websites, quizzes, polls and small games tied to their Bluesky identity.
story.title: Bluesky opens its Attie app so anyone can build sites and games with AI
story.why: It is a social network betting that AI-built apps can become a new kind of post.

story.background: Burger King Japan runs the fast-food chain's restaurants and ordering app in Japan.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: More than 11 million records were exposed.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Contact details plus order history can make scams look genuine.

drivers.label: Big name
drivers.text: Burger King is a global fast-food brand.

story.happened: The company says unauthorized access happened between October 2 and 7 and was confirmed on October 13, TechRadar reports. Exposed data includes names, birth dates, genders, emails, phone numbers and order histories. Payment card data was not exposed.

story.next: Watch for notices to affected customers and any phishing that uses the leaked details.
story.summary: Names, birth dates, contact details and order histories, mostly from app users, were exposed in early October.
story.title: Burger King Japan discloses a breach of 11.18 million customer records
story.why: Millions of real names and phone numbers in one leak make convincing phishing much easier.

story.background: The testing provider runs statewide assessments for California under contract with the state.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: About 7 million students are affected.

drivers.label: Risk
drivers.text: Disability status is among the most sensitive data exposed.

story.happened: An unauthorized party used a compromised credential to copy files between May 22 and September 18, DataBreaches.net reports. The data covers students over the past three school years. The California Department of Education announced the breach.

meme.take: A testing contractor's login was copied for four months before anyone checked the logs.

story.next: Watch for how families will be notified and what support is offered.
story.summary: A compromised login at testing provider Education Testing Service exposed names, addresses, demographics and disability status.
story.title: Hack exposes data on about 7 million California public school students
story.why: It is one of the largest breaches of student records, and it involves children's data.

story.background: Citizen Lab is a research group at the University of Toronto that investigates spyware.

drivers.text: Infection needed no click, only an ad loading.

drivers.label: Scale
drivers.text: The ad network reached about 200,000 apps and websites.

drivers.label: Controversy

meme.bottom: Finally, an ad that does what it says

story.next: Watch for Citizen Lab's follow-up report on a second group using the same ad system.

story.summary: Citizen Lab says malicious ads bought through Discover-Tech infected at least 45 devices of Al Jazeera journalists without a click.
story.title: Researchers say an ad network was used to plant Candiru spyware on journalists' phones
story.why: Zero-click spyware delivered through ordinary ads means anyone seeing an ad could be a target.

story.background: Cisco is one of the largest makers of networking and security equipment for businesses.

drivers.text: Cisco gear is used by many large companies and governments.

drivers.text: Attacks began weeks after fixes quietly shipped.
